section_summary.extract_value: This section describes hierarchical multiple regression analyses testing whether body appreciation predicts sexual function (Hypothesis 2) and whether BMI moderates the relationship between body appreciation and sexual function (Hypothesis 3). Results indicated that body appreciation significantly predicted sexual arousal, sexual satisfaction, orgasm, and overall sexual function after controlling for age and partner status, supporting Hypothesis 2. However, BMI did not significantly moderate these relationships, so Hypothesis 3 was not supported.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents hierarchical multiple regression analyses (Table 2) testing whether body appreciation predicts sexual function outcomes (FSFI subscales and full scale) above and beyond age and partner status, and whether BMI moderates this relationship. The study included 246 female participants. Results indicated that body appreciation significantly predicted sexual arousal, satisfaction, orgasm, and overall sexual function after controlling for age and partner status, supporting Hypothesis 2. However, BMI did not significantly moderate these relationships, so Hypothesis 3 was not supported.
